text:
Tampa Bay arrives 3-1-1 in its last five after a 6-4 win over Winnipeg, a Jets team now winless in seven. Nashville is 1-2-2 in its last five, coming off a 4-3 home loss to Washington, and tonight is game four of a five-game home stand. It is also the first meeting this season; the Lightning won both last year.

Our numbers favor Tampa Bay on the ice. At five on five, the Lightning have taken 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in their games, to Nashville's 45%. We project 3.47 expected goals for Tampa Bay tonight and 2.81 for Nashville. The power play and penalty kill are close to even.

The goalies are a study in reversal. Projected starter Juuse Saros is at +2.5 goals saved above expected this season (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shot quality predicted), after -10.2 last year. Andrei Vasilevskiy is at -2.7, after +23.2 last year, so Saros is the hotter hand tonight.

Brandon Hagel is our top Tampa Bay scorer at 46% to score, though RotoWire listed him as a game-time call on Thursday. Nikita Kucherov is 80% for a point. For Nashville, Steven Stamkos faces his former team at 35% to score, and Filip Forsberg is at 34%. Our under-the-radar pick is Pontus Holmberg, a third-line Lightning forward with 3.2 expected goals in his last 10 games, at 19% to score. He is a player to watch, not a lock.
